passive/checked-out at first (still gripping the TV remote through the whole scene, never puts it down)
quick with a dry, cutting one-liner once he engages
not visibly jealous or hurt, more amused/incredulous at his wife's excuse
emotional_range: mock incredulity / comedic outrage played for laughs, not real anger

characters.interactions_notes: He is physically closer to the TV/background and slower to engage, establishing him as the reactive partner rather than the instigator. He does not make eye contact until she confesses, then holds a steady, almost interrogating stare while pointing at her, which combined with his flat vocal delivery signals he's turning her confession into a joke rather than a real fight. He never touches her or the phone, keeping a clear physical/comedic distance that reinforces the couple's the-joke-is-on-you dynamic.

personality_traits: impulsive confessor -- blurts out the embarrassing admission unprompted
self-aware and mildly panicked about the social fallout ('she got a notification')
fidgety with her phone, using it as a nervous prop throughout
ultimately unbothered/amused by the end, suggesting she treats the mishap lightly despite the initial panic

0:05-0:06 mouth open mid-word, eyes darting, visibly rattled as she keeps talking

characters.interactions_notes: She initiates the whole exchange, speaking first and unprompted, positioning her as the one who disrupts the couple's quiet TV-watching routine. She keeps her eyes mostly on her phone or glancing sideways at him rather than fully facing him, reflecting embarrassment. The power dynamic flips over the course of the beat: she starts in control of the reveal (confessing on her own terms) but ends up the target of his punchline, visible in her softened, slightly sheepish smile at the close as he gets the last word.
